results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Floor Press
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your legs straight on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your arm extended straight up towards the ceiling, palm facing forward. Keep your free hand on the floor for support.
Lower the dumbbell by bending your elbow until your upper arm touches the floor, bringing your elbow at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the dumbbell back up to the starting position by extending your elbow, squeezing your chest at the top of the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Avoid letting your back arch off the floor; keep it flat and supported.
Focus on using your chest and triceps to lift the dumbbell.
Keep your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm during the exercise.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Floor Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Wide Grip Bench Press
instructions: Begin by lying flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand, extending your arm straight above your shoulder, with a wide grip and palm facing forward.
Lower the dumbbell slowly towards the floor by bending your elbow, until your elbow passes lower than the bench.
Push the dumbbell back up to the starting position by extending your arm, squeezing your chest muscles at the top of the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Focus on a slow and controlled movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Keep your wrist straight to avoid unnecessary strain.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Wide Grip Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Single Arm Floor Press From Close Elbow
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand, positioning your arm close to your body with your elbow touching the floor and bent at a 90-degree angle.
Press the dumbbell up by extending your arm until it is fully straightened towards the ceiling.
Lower the dumbbell back down with control, bringing your elbow back to the starting position close to your body and touching the floor.
Complete the desired number of repetitions with the right arm, then switch to the left arm and repeat the movement.
tips: Maintain a neutral wrist position throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the dumbbell up and inhale as you lower it.
Ensure your non-working arm is firm on the floor for support.
results.description: Dumbbell Single Arm Floor Press From Close Elbow is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Single Arm Floor Press
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with your arm bent and your elbow touching the floor, at a 45-degree angle from your body.
Press the dumbbell up by extending your arm until it is fully straightened towards the ceiling.
Lower the dumbbell back down with control, bringing your elbow back to a few inches off the floor.
Complete the desired number of repetitions with the right arm, then switch to the left arm and repeat the movement.
tips: Maintain a neutral wrist position throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the dumbbell up and inhale as you lower it.
Ensure your non-working arm is firm on the floor for support.
results.description: Dumbbell Single Arm Floor Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Standing Single Arm Cross Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand with a neutral grip. Extend your right arm straight down at your side. Your left hand should be on your hip for support.
Raise the dumbbell diagonally across your body towards your left shoulder, keeping your arm straight and maintaining a slight bend in your elbow.
Hold the position briefly at the top, ensuring the dumbbell reaches shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, keeping your movements slow and steady. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Exhale as you raise the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow to reduce strain on your joints.
results.description: Dumbbell Standing Single Arm Cross Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest.

results.name: Dumbbell Svend Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell with both hands. Position the dumbbell vertically in front of your chest with your palms facing each other and your fingers interlocked.
Engage your chest and press the dumbbells together with your palms, activating your chest muscles.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, keeping the dumbbell pressed together in your palms.
Bring the dumbbell back to your chest. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain constant pressure on the dumbbell to activate your chest muscles effectively.
Avoid locking your elbows at the end of the extension; keep a slight bend.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell Svend Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Elevated Push Up
instructions: Place your hands on elevated surfaces just wider than shoulder-width apart. Position your feet together on the floor, forming a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core and lower your chest towards the elevated surfaces by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle from your body.
Lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor between the elevated surfaces, maintaining a straight back and tight core throughout the movement.
Push through your hands to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with control, lowering yourself slowly to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Avoid flaring your elbows out to the sides; keep them at a 45-degree angle to engage your chest and triceps more effectively.
results.description: Elevated Push Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Explosive Push Ups
instructions: Begin in a standard push-up position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping your core tight and your body straight.
Push through your hands explosively to extend your arms rapidly, generating maximum force without lifting your hands off the floor.
Lower into the next push-up with control, immediately repeating the explosive movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your movements controlled and focus on generating power in the push without lifting off the floor.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up explosively and inhaling as you lower down.
Focus on explosive power and control rather than speed to maximize effectiveness.
Use a non-slip surface to prevent your hands from slipping during the exercise.
results.description: Explosive Push Ups is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Flat Bench Cable Fly
instructions: Position a flat bench between two cable machines with the pulleys set at the lowest position. Attach handles to the pulleys and lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing up, and extend your arms out to your sides at chest level.
Raise the handles over your chest in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, squeezing your chest at the top.
Slowly bring the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to avoid straining your joints.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Inhale as you lower the handles back down and exhale as you raise them up.
results.description: Flat Bench Cable Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Floor Cable Resistance Band Press
instructions: Lie on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Position a resistance band under your upper back, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing forward.
Position your elbows on the floor bent at a 90-degree angle.
Press the handles straight up towards the ceiling until your arms are fully extended, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the handles up and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Floor Cable Resistance Band Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.
